text.p: Lockheed Martin Corp on Wednesday said the state of Florida approved a one-year extension of its contract to track down parents who have failed to make child-support payments and to collect the overdue payments from them.
Lockheed Martin -- one of the two companies named to
enforce child-support verdicts last January -- said it collected $15.3 million from parents who were at least six months behind on their child-support payments during 1996.

The value of the contract is based upon how much is collected from the parents, but all of the child support goes to custodial parents and their children or to the state to recoup welfare costs, Lockheed Martin said.
Lockheed Martin receives a fee from the Florida Department of Revenue, which is reimbursed by the federal government, the company said.

Lockheed Martin and RSI, the other company, get a fee equal to 16 percent of the amount they collect from the parents that have failed to make child support payments, according to Florida's Department of Revenue.
